ABSTRACT: We examine whether financial markets expect stablecoins to
play an important role in payments. After the decisive congressional vote
on the GENIUS Act, the market value of payment incumbents fell by 1.3%
($21.5 billion) relative to other financial firms, consistent with stablecoins
increasing competition in payments. The decline was larger for firms
focused on cross-border payments, and smaller for those protected by
network effects or offering crypto services. Accounting for anticipation using
prediction markets, we estimate that the Act reduced the value of incumbent
payment firms by 13–27% ($220–470 billion), exceeding the impact of
recent pro-competitive regulatory shocks.
